title: Atlas Core portable recovery destination security assessment
scope: Provider-neutral encrypted local-folder destination, automation, SDK and Gateway receipts, operator visibility, retention, and recovery import

approved_targets: Disposable local folders, databases, and encrypted artifacts
Loopback operator and Gateway test services
prohibited_actions: Choose or write to a real off-device destination
Store a real recovery passphrase in source, config, receipts, or logs
Install a service, scheduled task, or startup action
Restore a live Company Memory database

trust_boundaries: Verified local backup to encrypted portable artifact
Runtime secret source to in-process encryption and authentication
Payload-free receipt to SDK, Gateway, and localhost operator
data_flows: Verified SQLite backup to AES-256-GCM and scrypt artifact
Exclusive partial write to same-directory artifact and manifest replacement
Encrypted read-back to authentication and plaintext checksum verification
Portable receipt to automation ledger and read-only status surfaces
Authenticated portable artifact to registered local recovery point

threats.name: Passphrase persisted or exposed by configuration
threats.control: Configuration accepts only a validated environment-variable name, rejects unknown fields such as passphrase, prompts without echo for attended launcher use, and never records the value

threats.name: Partial, corrupt, or tampered copy reported as usable
threats.control: Exclusive partial files, fsync, same-directory replacement, SHA-256 verification, authenticated decryption, backup identity check, and plaintext checksum check precede success

threats.name: Arbitrary path or linked destination traversal
threats.control: Explicit absolute destination resolution, filesystem-root rejection, identifier allowlists, filename construction from validated export IDs, and symlink/junction rejection

threats.name: Unattended deletion removes all recovery copies
threats.control: Retention defaults to preview, preserves invalid entries, enforces at least two valid copies, and requires an exact destination-specific confirmation

threats.name: Remote or browser surface discloses destination or secret
threats.control: Receipts expose only safe identifiers, filenames, hashes, sizes, algorithms, and outcomes; Gateway redacts configuration/state paths and offers no destination mutation API

findings.finding: A process or device failure after artifact replacement but before manifest replacement can leave an orphan encrypted artifact. Atlas refuses to overwrite it, requiring operator inspection instead of silently treating it as valid.
The adapter secures Atlas artifact handling but cannot prove that a mounted or synchronized folder is physically off-device, durable, private, or governed by an approved provider policy.

validation: Six focused portable destination tests passed in the installed Atlas Python environment
Seventy-four full-suite tests, Python compilation, and operator JavaScript syntax passed
Rebuilt three-wheel installed-package smoke authenticated a portable copy and returned portable_exported through the remote SDK
Live localhost operator rendered verified portable status with no secret or path disclosure, no console errors, and no horizontal overflow
residual_risk: No real portable or off-device destination has been selected, mounted, authorized, or tested.
Runtime secret custody, rotation, escrow, and recovery ceremony remain deployment-owner responsibilities.
Directory ancestry and synchronized-provider behavior depend on the selected deployment and require live validation.
This assessment is implementation evidence, not a compliance certification.
